newsitem.title: USA: Southern sets Consolidated Electric Power Asia bid.
newsitem.headline: Southern sets Consolidated Electric Power Asia bid.

text.p: Southern Co will offer HK$18.50, about US$2.39, for each Consolidated Electric Power Asia share under its agreement to purchase 80 percent of the company, spokesman Chuck Griffin said on Wednesday.

The cost will total $2.7 billion with $600 million being funded by Consolidated Electric funds on hand in the form of a dividend, he said in response to questions about the agreement announced four-and-a-half hours earlier.
Under Southern's agreement with Hopewell Holdings Ltd, owner of 60.4 percent of Consolidated Electric, Hopewell will tender 80 percent of its shares.

Southern chief executive A.W. Dahlberg explained Hopewell has agreed to elect a second, "combination option" available to all Consolidated Electric shareholders to tender 80 percent of their stock for an immediate cash payment of $16.50 a share plus a contingency payment of $2 per share when an Indonesian power plant under construction is completed.

He told an analysts' teleconference Wednesday election of the second option by all shareholders would reduce Hopewell's stake in Consolidated Electric to 12.1 percent, while election of the first option by all other holders would leave Hopewell with 20 percent, adding that is the "likely" result.

He said the transaction "should close this year," noting it is subject to approval by the Stock Exchange of Hong Kong, Consolidated Electric shareholders and the courts in Bermuda, where the company is incorporated.
Chief Financial Officer Larry Westbrook told the analysts Southern's net cost of $2.1 billion will be financed initially with bank debt which will be refinanced with non-recourse debt and equity.
He said the equity will be contributed over three years until it accounts for 60 percent of the price.
"Our plan (is to contribute the equity) through cash flow to reduce the need to issue new shares," he said.
Westbrook said the exact financing schedule will be determined early next year.
